stories.headline: Astronomers found the 1st green star ever seen
stories.summary: White dwarf WD J1330+6435 swallowed rocky debris from its old planets. Sodium in its dense atmosphere absorbs orange light, so to human eyes it would glow a ghostly green.
stories.why: No star, living or dead, had ever been credibly reported as green.

stories.headline: A deep-sea canyon off Argentina held 57 new species
stories.summary: Taxonomists found 57 new species and 5 new genera, including a horned sea cucumber nicknamed Loki, 2,577 m down. Of the copepods checked, every single one was new to science.
stories.why: Over 4 million people watched the dives live, and the deep sea still hides more.

stories.headline: A gene therapy helped blind patients find objects again
stories.summary: In a trial for advanced retinitis pigmentosa, one injection made surviving eye cells sense light. With special goggles, 7 of 10 patients saw more light, and some found doors and objects.
stories.why: It works whatever the faulty gene, so one approach could help many forms of blindness.

stories.stat_label: years old, and gene switches look young
stories.headline: A 194-year-old tortoise has gene switches that look young
stories.summary: Scientists read the DNA of Jonathan, the oldest known land animal. Gene switches for energy and DNA repair looked like a 5-year-old tortoise's, and he carries 287 unusual gene variants.
stories.why: Clues from a near-200-year-old could guide research into healthy ageing.

fun_fact: Jonathan arrived on St Helena in 1882, already fully grown.
